Uses and Administration Purified talc is used in massage and as a dusting pow- der to allay irritation and prevent chafing. It is usually mixed with starch, to increase absorption of moisture, and zinc oxide. Talc used in dusting powders should be sterilised. Purified talc is used as a lubricant and diluent in making tablets and capsules and to clarify liquids. Sterile purified talc is also used as a sclerosant after drainage of malignant pleural effusion and for recur- rent spontaneous pneumothorax. It is administered into the pleural cavity as a slurry or by aerosol (insuffla- tion). Doses of about 5 g may be used for pleural effu- sion and 2 g for pneumothorax. Pleural effusions. Talc is used as a sclerosant to achieve pleu- rodesis in the management of benign and malignant pleural effu- sions (p.659) and recurrent spontaneous pneumothorax.1-4 It is generally given into the pleural space as a slurry via intercostal tube, or by insufflation (talc poudrage) at thoracoscopy.
